dataset.name: Iron-mediated oxidation of methoxyhydroquinone at the Rifle Floodplain, Colorado
description: In this study, the oxidation of 2-methoxyhydroquinone (MH2Q) by ferric iron (Fe(III)) under dark conditions in the absence and presence of oxygen was investigated within a pH range of 4 – 6. While Fe(III) was capable of stoichiometrically oxidizing MH2Q under anaerobic conditions, catalytic oxidation of MH2Q was observed in the presence of O2 due to further cycling between oxygen, semiquinone radicals, and iron species. A detailed kinetic model was developed to describe the predominant mechanisms, which indicated that both the undissociated and mono-dissociated anions of MH2Q were kinetically active species towards Fe(III) reduction, with the mono-dissociated anion being the key species accounting for the pH dependence of the oxidation. The generated radical intermediates, namely semiquinone and superoxide, are of great importance in reaction chain propagation. The kinetic model may provide critical insight into the underlying mechanisms of the thermodynamic and kinetic characteristics of metal-organic interactions and assist in understanding and predicting the factors controlling iron and organic matter transformation and bioavailability in aquatic systems.

spatialCoverage.description: Site: Rifle, Colorado US-RIF. The Rifle site is located in the east side of the Upper Colorado River Basin (UCRB) in northwestern Colorado. The site had a former uranium and vanadium mill, which operated between 1924 and 1958. As a uranium‐contaminated site it has been the focus of several intense hydrological, biogeochemical, and bioremediation research activities., and was used by the DOE Sustainable Systems Scientific Focus Area to explore how climate drivers influence hydrological processes and biogeochemical cycling within the Colorado River Basin. The Rifle site is located atop a floodplain adjacent to the Colorado River floodplain systems within the UCRB, and is representative of floodplains in the UCRB based upon its overall aquifer properties and hydrological coupling to the Colorado River.

measurementTechnique:
(a) Measurement of 2-methoxybenzoquinone (MBQ): Concentrations of MBQ were determined spectrophotometrically using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with ε257 = 1.48 × 104 M−1 cm−1.
(b) Fe(II) Determination: Concentrations of total Fe(II) were determined using a modified Ferrozine method.
(c) H2O2 Determination: H2O2 concentrations were determined by the chemiluminescing reaction between acridinium ester (AE, 10-methyl-9-(p-formylphenyl)-acridinium carboxylate trifluoromethanesulfonate) and the conjugate base of H2O2 (HO2−, pKa = 11.6). The emitted luminescence at 470 nm was detected by flow injection analysis using a FeLume system (Waterville Analytical, Waterville, ME).
